doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Playing Real Book tunes in Ernie Krivda's basement
summary: As a teenager he played trumpet, tenor and drums with Ernie Krivda and Val Kent, walking bass lines, and urges students to do the same.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I am definitely surrounded by all music and art. And like I said before, I thought everybody’s house had music and live music in it all the time you know. And that would be wonderful, that would be great for kids. You know when I was growing up I would play with this tenor player, Ernie Krivda from Cleveland, and Val Kent, a drummer. The © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-

three of us were real close. And we’d go to Ernie’s house in his basement and we would play out of the Real Book, and we would play tunes just me and Ernie, no bass just drums and tenor and trumpet. And we’d play tune after tune after tune and we’d just, that’s how we learned to play there you know, in the basement, learning tunes and stuff. And I think that’s very, very important, outside of school for these students to get together, form a band, play tunes. You know you don’t need a — it’s really good with just a trumpet and tenor and drums.
Yeah you’ve got to make your own harmony and etcetera.

Absolutely. Just playing. I played a bass line, I walked a bass line when the tenor would play the solo and then he would walk a bass line when I’d solo. Very, very good, it’s a great experience and I think they’d learn a lot from that. That’s things that they can do that they can’t get in school.
